prize_parts.citation: for the invention and development of optical lattice clocks based on magic-wavelength trapping, which brought time and frequency measurement to unprecedented accuracy

statement.case_for: Having read all eight opening ballots, I move my preferred configuration from IceCube (B061), my opening first place, to optical lattice clocks (B010). B010 is the only candidate ranked by six members, with two first places, and no member who ranked it gave it a weak assessment. The discovery is concrete and original: Katori's magic-wavelength proposal removes the light-shift perturbation of the clock transition, so that many atoms can be interrogated at once. Ye's group then took the scheme to fractional uncertainties near 1e-18, beyond the caesium definition of the second, and used it for tests of fundamental constants and of relativistic redshift over millimetre distances. Independent laboratories have reproduced and surpassed the performance, and the redefinition of the second is under discussion, so recognition is timely. The two-person credit is the cleanest attribution on the shortlist, and nobody proposed any other pair for it. I would rank it ahead of my own field's candidate because the case is stronger across the whole committee, not because the IceCube result is weak.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is territorial and conceptual. The 2005 prize (frequency comb) and the 2012 prize (ion control and ion clocks) cover adjacent ground, and the committee could judge that a lattice-clock prize rewards a further stage of precision metrology rather than a new phenomenon. The credit also leaves out ion-clock pioneers and other lattice-clock groups, and the relative weight of Katori's proposal against Ye's accuracy milestones is a judgement I cannot settle from the supplied evidence. If the committee wants a discovery of nature in preference to a measurement advance, B051 or B061 would fit that wish better.

responses.point: Kroll ranks B010 first as a decisive advance in how accurately we can measure frequency, with Katori and Ye as the natural pair, and notes that ion-clock and comb work already recognised in 2005 might be seen as part of the same story.
responses.response: I agree with the pair and with the metrology criterion. I take the 2005 and 2012 overlap more seriously than your ballot does, though. The citation must be written around the magic-wavelength lattice, which neither earlier prize covers, and not around clocks in general. If the committee cannot accept that distinction, B010 loses much of its edge. I think the distinction holds, because many neutral atoms interrogated at once is a different route to stability, not a refinement of ion clocks.

responses.point: Lindroth ranks B010 first and also gives B047 and B058 high places. She treats Katori's proposal and Ye's accuracy programme as a clean two-laureate fit and sees recognition as timely even though the redefinition of the second is still in progress.
responses.response: I agree that the pairing is clean and that the pending redefinition does not weaken the science. I would resist her high placing of B058, however. Quantum key distribution is a protocol insight rather than a physical discovery, several members say so, and the 2022 prize already covers its foundational neighbourhood. I would therefore not put B058 in a combined slate with B010. B047 is a serious competitor, and my reason for preferring B010 is attribution, not scientific merit.

responses.point: Mehlig ranks B047 first, calling the Z2 invariant and the quantum spin Hall state a reorganisation of how phases are classified. He regards the maturity as overdue and the Kane, Mele and Molenkamp trio as defensible, while leaving out the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal and Hasan's 3D work.
responses.response: The conceptual weight of topological insulators is higher than that of any other shortlisted candidate, and I do not dispute it. My reservation is allocation. Six of seven supporters propose Kane, Mele and Molenkamp, but Danielsson would include Hasan and drop Mele. Several ballots flag the missing Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang proposal, and Zhang cannot be recognised posthumously. A prize that excludes the HgTe prediction while crediting its experimental confirmation will be criticised on priority. I also think the 2016 overlap is smaller than some colleagues suggest, but it has to be argued. B047 stays my first alternative if the attribution can be solved.

responses.point: Danielsson ranks the magic-angle graphene candidate B051 first as a concrete, original discovery with a natural theory-plus-experiment trio, and ranks IceCube third.
responses.response: I ranked B051 second and agree it has the widest support, with all eight members ranking it. I place it behind B010 for two reasons that your own ballot notes. The pairing mechanism for the superconductivity is unsettled, and the credit omits the first author Yuan Cao and other early groups, so the attribution is less secure than for the clocks. On IceCube, you describe the source identification as partial, and I admit that my own ballot overstated how settled it is. Only one experiment has confirmed the diffuse flux so far, and only three members ranked B061. For those reasons I keep it as an alternative and no longer as my lead.

responses.point: Johansson ranks circuit QED first, with a stated bias toward his own subfield, and asks whether another superconducting-circuit prize so soon after 2025 is wise.
responses.response: I appreciate the declared bias, and I rank B041 third myself, but I think the 2025 prize counts against it more than your ballot allows. Girvin and Huang were co-authors of the proposal, so the trio of names is not a clean allocation, and the 2025 laureates include Devoret, whose Yale-linked programme overlaps. I would not take B041 forward now. Your ranking of Cirac and Zoller (B046) is a stronger idea, but it was ranked by only three members.

uncertainties: Whether the 2005 and 2012 prizes make lattice clocks look like incremental metrology, rather than a distinct prize-worthy invention.
Whether Katori and Ye can be credited without ion-clock pioneers and other lattice-clock groups, and the relative weight of proposal against accuracy milestones.
Whether B047 attribution can be settled among Kane, Mele, Molenkamp, Hasan and the uncredited Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang, since B047 would otherwise compete strongly.
Whether the pairing mechanism and the Cao and other-group credit issues would leave B051 too early, which I treat as uncertain.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for B010 or any other shortlisted candidate. My documented connections are to PAMELA, Fermi-LAT, PoGOLite/PoGO+ and XL-Calibur, none involving the credited names. My field is astroparticle physics, which is adjacent to B061 (IceCube), so I have discounted my own opening advocacy of that candidate and would stand back from any final decision on it if the committee requested.
